QEVA HARVESTER 0.2 · METADATA FIRST

Collect sources without confusing access, permission, or truth.

This release contains a bounded reference harvester with byte ceilings, atomic storage, raw fixity checks, immutable provider assertions, rights-gated candidate extraction, and explicit checkpoints. It does not claim a bulk crawl or a complete corpus.

The only safe direction of travel.

  1. Discover
    APIs, snapshots, OAI feeds, crawl indexes
  2. Preserve
    raw bytes, request, time, media type, hash
  3. Normalize
    works, identifiers, authors, dates, rights
  4. Resolve
    DOI, arXiv, title/year/author fingerprints
  5. Extract
    candidate claims, definitions, equations, problems
  6. Qualify
    human or formal review before the logical archive

RUN IT

Small, bounded, and fail-closed by default.

Python's standard library is enough for the reference implementation. Each distinct retrieval stores raw bytes and a content-addressed ledger event before normalization; an exact repeat coalesces to the same event ID. Completed outputs are deterministic, while page-level crash resumption remains future work. Run from dist/; outputs go beside—not inside—the immutable release.

# deterministic offline proof that the pipeline works
python3 -B harvester/harvest.py demo --out ../qeva-work/demo-run

# bounded live metadata queries
python3 -B harvester/harvest.py fetch openalex "dynamical systems" --limit 100 --out ../qeva-work/openalex
python3 -B harvester/harvest.py fetch crossref "prime number theorem" --limit 100 --mailto you@example.org --out ../qeva-work/crossref
python3 -B harvester/harvest.py fetch arxiv "cat:math.DS" --limit 100 --out ../qeva-work/arxiv

# discover URLs in a Common Crawl index; content is not downloaded
python3 -B harvester/harvest.py fetch commoncrawl "math.example.edu/*" --limit 100 --out ../qeva-work/commoncrawl

# extract clearly labelled candidates; every result remains unreviewed
python3 -B harvester/harvest.py extract ../qeva-work/arxiv/normalized.jsonl --out ../qeva-work/arxiv/candidates.jsonl

SOURCE FAMILIES

Use bulk infrastructure before direct crawling.

Terms, licenses, and API behavior change. The registry records the current strategy, but every production run must capture the terms and rights basis it actually used.

BIBLIOGRAPHIC

OpenAlex

Broad works, authors, institutions, topics, and citation graph. Use filtered API runs for development and snapshots for real scale.

API + snapshot

BIBLIOGRAPHIC

Crossref

DOIs, references, licenses, updates, and retractions. Metadata is open in general; abstracts can carry separate rights.

REST + annual data file

REPOSITORY

arXiv

Modern research metadata through API/OAI and bulk infrastructure. Each article file retains its own submission license.

API + OAI-PMH + S3

WEB DISCOVERY

Common Crawl

Search the CDXJ or URL index before fetching WARC/WET content. Presence in a crawl grants no redistribution license.

index first; content later

MATH INDEX

zbMATH Open

Mathematics-specific classifications, reviews, identities, and citations under its current API terms.

API + OAI-PMH

SPECIALIZED CORPUS

OEIS

Sequences, formulas, transforms, and references. Preserve CC BY-SA attribution and share-alike; never relabel it CC0.

bulk files · CC BY-SA

KNOWLEDGE GRAPH

Wikidata

People, works, dates, identifiers, and historical reconciliation. Linked media and cited sources can have different rights.

dumps + SPARQL

DIGITAL LIBRARY

Internet Archive

Historical scans, books, and metadata. Rights vary per item and per file.

metadata + item APIs

FORMAL LIBRARY

Mathlib

Machine-checked declarations and real import dependencies tied to repository commits and declaration names.

Git + generated declarations

HISTORY

MacTutor

A curated orientation source and lead generator. Cite it; do not absorb its prose as QEVA-native text.

reference layer

FRONTIER STATUS

Clay Mathematics Institute

An official source for the Millennium Problem statements and resolution status.

reference layer

FAIL-CLOSED RIGHTS

Accessible does not mean redistributable.

The harvester defaults to metadata-only. Full text requires an explicit item-level rights basis. Unknown is stored as unknown—not guessed open.

THE CORPUS MAY STORE

identifiers, title, authors, dates, citations, retrieval event, raw hash, rights signal, normalized factual structure, and a canonical locator where lawful.

THE LOGICAL ARCHIVE MAY ADMIT

only a qualified mathematical object with explicit assumptions, exact dependencies, status, provenance, and enough information to challenge it.

THE REAL SCALE PLAN

Snapshots → indexes → selective bytes → candidates.

Do not make billions of polite API calls when a provider offers a snapshot. Do not download a web corpus before querying its URL index. Do not run extraction before storing provenance. Do not promote extraction to truth.

  • OpenAlex / CrossrefSNAPSHOTS
  • arXivOAI + BULK
  • Broad webCOMMON CRAWL INDEX
  • Missing high-value sourcesSELECTIVE CRAWL
  • Logical graph admissionQUALIFICATION
QEVACorpus provenance is not logical truth.
